doc.title: Ray Vega interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, July 20, 2023

title: 1975 pop hits, High School of Music & Art and early classical and jazz listening
summary: Rowe lists 1975 hits; Vega says he was a freshman at Music & Art discovering Parker, Dizzy and Freddie Hubbard, loving brass recordings, with teacher Sidney Baker.

venues.name: High School of Music and Art

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Growing up with radio, records and family listening

blocks.x: I was going to ask you about that. You were born in 1961 is that correct?
So I picked sort of an arbitrary time, 1975 you would have been around 14 and I looked at the top songs. 1975. Number 1 — “Love Will Keep Us Together” by Captain & Tennille.
Captain & Tennille, I remember that pop radio.
And down at Number 22 was “The Hustle.”

Oh yeah. I grew up listening to all that music. Well hearing it. I was hearing it in the background ‘cause I had family members that really loved that stuff. But at that time, in 1975, I was at the time, I started out at the High School of Music & Art. I was a freshman at that time, and I was discovering Charlie Parker and Dizzy and Freddie Hubbard. That’s what I was getting into. I was also really into classical music so I was discovering some

wonderful recordings like there’s a recording of the Philadelphia, New York, and I want to say Chicago Symphony brass sections playing the Gabrieli Canzon. It was a very famous recording that was put out by I want to say RCA. And I had a really good trumpet teacher in high school named Sidney Baker who was from that tradition. So you just, when you’re around it that’s what you know. And mind you, this is before the Internet. So if you wanted to really seek out information you had to really put some — you had to make a real effort. You have to make a real effort. Sorry, my dog just moved this. Stay there. Sorry about that, Monk.
It’s okay, we are doing home studio today.
